A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRES research work, renamed from HDC to CoHD. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; the localized Ref-ZOM metric-label ambiguity is noted below.

before.justification: v1 reports original HDC segmentation and counting results on GRES and RES benchmarks, together with component ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original CoHD benchmark results, combined-dataset training results, and selection, decoder-depth, and computational-cost analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces Multi-level Mask Aggregation with Dynamic Hierarchical Aggregation. v1 projects each level into a two-class mask before aggregation with fixed weights; v2 introduces learned inter-level gates and intra-level channel attention, aggregates the semantic maps, and then performs the final projection. The underlying semantic attention, query refinement, and counting objectives largely survive their renaming.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate gRefCOCO, Ref-ZOM, R-RefCOCO/+/g, and RefCOCO/+/g with the same single-, multiple-, and empty-target task coverage. Combining retained RES datasets for training changes the protocol rather than introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds DMMI to the gRefCOCO comparison in Table 1, although it already appeared on other benchmarks in v1. The RES comparison adds RISCLIP and PolyFormer, while the decoder comparison drops Mask Attn. Most existing comparators, including LISA and GSVA, remain.

E3.justification: v1 reports separate-dataset RES training; v2 Table 3 adds combined-dataset training evaluated with mIoU alongside single-dataset oIoU results. New experiments introduce two-, three-, and four-layer decoder configurations and parameter/FLOP measurements. These are additional evaluation designs; the shared optimizer, batch size, image resolution, and text-length settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds intra-/inter-selection ablations, decoder-depth sensitivity, and efficiency-versus-performance analysis (Tables 5, 12, and 13). It revises the HSD component tests and activation-map examples, while removing v1's isolated language-reactivation test, fixed aggregation-weight sweep, and mask-attention comparison. The analytical evidence is substantially reorganized around the revised decoder.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix E reports several retrainings on gRefCOCO and a 'standard variation' of approximately 0.36, without specifying the exact run count or associated metric. v2 removes this statement and supplies no replacement uncertainty reporting. This establishes a reporting removal, not a change in how many runs were performed.

E6.justification: Results change across the retained benchmarks: Swin-B gRefCOCO validation/test-B gIoU changes from 68.28/63.85 to 68.42/63.60, while R-RefCOCOg rIoU changes from 43.85 to 42.16. v2 also adds combined-RES, selection, depth, and efficiency results. Ref-ZOM accuracy remains 93.34 despite the corrected introductory improvement margin. Its IoU headings reverse between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 10 while baseline values retain their column positions, making the corresponding metric changes ambiguous.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of aggregation changes substantively: v1 Equations 7-8 are replaced by gating, channel-attention, and aggregation-before-projection definitions in v2 Equations 7-11. The attention, counting-loss, and existence-head formulations otherwise remain essentially equivalent. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain hierarchical decoding plus explicit counting for GRES and superiority over existing approaches. v2 refines the decoding contribution to emphasize dynamic intra-/inter-selection and removes v1's explicit claim to be the first to introduce object counting into GRES. The overall task and contribution scope remain stable.

C2.justification: v2 Section 7.1 newly explains smaller RES gains through simpler referring scenarios and smaller training datasets, presenting joint training as a partial remedy. It also adds interpretations of selective aggregation and insufficient or excessive decoder depth. The limitation concerning truncation to 20 text tokens is retained.

D1.justification: v2 Section 6.3 explains constructing counting labels from existing COCO annotations and using 12 super-categories; v1 did not document this construction explicitly. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed labels. v2 also reports parameter/FLOP costs and describes code as available rather than forthcoming, with an updated repository link. Most training and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Mixtral of Experts, ECA-Net, RISCLIP, and PolyFormer, removes the Mask2Former reference, and expands the explanation of GSVA's relationship to LISA. It also drops the first-counting-in-GRES priority assertion. The broader positioning against existing GRES decoding approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative undergo substantial rewriting, with HDC/MAC renamed CoHD/AOC and STM/STQ consolidated under Semantic Decoding Module terminology. RES results move into the main text, Ref-ZOM results move into the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized. The Error Bar and Broader Impacts sections are removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the central architecture diagrams, restructures several ablation tables, and expands the RES table into separate training settings. v1's three-scenario bubble plot becomes v2 Table 6, and the activation-map examples are replaced. Several segmentation panels are retained with changed placement and numbering.

improvement.justification: The counting-label explanation and targeted selection, depth, and cost analyses make implementation and design tradeoffs easier to assess. These provide a limited net improvement over v1's already broad empirical evaluation. The gain is tempered by removal of the variability report and unexplained Ref-ZOM metric relabeling; the mixed benchmark updates do not establish uniform performance improvement.
